label: prf:ordering-jet-compatibility
title: Proof of ordering jet compatibility
html:
Proof. Proof of ordering jet compatibility

Proof. (1) Extension. At level n, the Hecke basis of A_n is a monomial basis B_n in the generators \sigma_1^{(n)}, \ldots, \sigma_{d_n - 1}^{(n)}. The jet prolongation A_{n+1} = A_n \otimes \Omega^1(A_n) introduces \dim(\Omega^1) = 3 new directions (in the \mathrm{SU}(2) case: \omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3). Define \prec_{n+1} by degree-lexicographic extension: monomials in B_n keep their relative order; new generators \omega_i are ordered after all level-n generators. This preserves the ordering on the image of \ell_n and well-orders the new monomials.

(2) Compatibility. The Frobenius–Hopf structure on A_{n+1} is inherited from A_n by jet prolongation (jet prolongation). The comultiplication \Delta_{n+1} and multiplication \mu_{n+1} satisfy the same Hecke relation T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1 at level n+1. Degree-lexicographic orderings are compatible with any associative multiplication whose defining relations have leading terms of bounded degree — the Hecke relation is quadratic, so this holds.

(3) Well-foundedness. The degree-lexicographic ordering on B_{n+1} is well-ordered because: (a) total degree is bounded below by 0; (b) at fixed degree, lexicographic ordering on a finite alphabet is well-ordered. The finiteness of the alphabet at each level is guaranteed by the Frobenius–Hopf axioms (the algebra is finitely generated at each level).

(4) Direct limit. For any a \in \mathcal{A}_\infty, there exists n such that a \in \mathrm{End}(A_n). The leading monomial \mathrm{LM}(a) is computed in B_n with respect to \prec_n. By (1), \mathrm{LM}(a) is the same whether computed in B_n or in B_m for any m \geq n — the embedding \ell_n preserves leading monomials. The Gröbner--Shirshov reduction algorithm applied to a in A_n terminates by (3); the same reduction is valid in \mathcal{A}_\infty. \square

Consequence for time. The braiding-induced ordering \prec_c on A_0 propagates through the entire jet tower. At every brane level, "forward time" (Gröbner--Shirshov reduction, braiding) and "backward time" (anti-involution, unbraiding) are well-defined and compatible with the algebraic structure. The arrow of time is inherited from the initial ordering; it does not need to be re-imposed at each level.
